message.reasoning:
I'm realizing the verifier is invalidating packet pointers after calling global functions like helper_a because those functions might internally call helpers like bpf_skb_pull_data that modify packet data, so even though the bounds check happened before the call, the register holding the packet pointer (R7 in this case) gets marked as scalar and loses its validity.

The fix is to reload the packet pointer and re-validate it after the global function call instead of relying on the pre-call bounds check. I'm moving the pointer dereference and bounds check to occur after helper_a returns, which gives the verifier a fresh packet pointer to work with.
